purpose: Testosterone cypionate is used to treat low testosterone levels in men, a condition sometimes called 'Low T' or hypogonadism. It helps restore testosterone to normal levels so you feel more like yourself again. It may also be used in some transgender men as part of hormone therapy.
how_it_works: Testosterone is the main male hormone your body naturally makes. When your body does not make enough on its own, this medication replaces it. It is injected into a muscle and slowly releases testosterone into your bloodstream over time, keeping your levels steady.
common_side_effects: Acne or oily skin, increased body or facial hair, mood changes or irritability, increased red blood cell count, pain or swelling at the injection site, fluid retention or mild swelling in the hands or feet, and changes in sex drive.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of blood clots, stroke, or heart attack, especially if you already have heart disease. It can cause your body to stop making its own testosterone if used long-term. It should never be used by women who are pregnant. Misuse or abuse can cause serious liver problems, mood swings, and dependence. Tell your doctor right away if you have chest pain, trouble breathing, or leg swelling.
typical_dosing: For most men with low testosterone, a common dose is 50 to 400 mg injected into a muscle every 2 to 4 weeks. Your doctor will find the right dose for you based on your blood levels. It is usually given at a clinic, but your doctor may teach you how to inject it at home.
